citations.title: Head of Popular Resistance Committees in Khan Yunis eliminated
citations.excerpt: The IDF and Israel Security Agency (Shin Bet) announced Thursday that they eliminated Ramadan Muhammad Ashahada Diab, the head of the Popular Resistance Committees terrorist organization in the Khan Yunis area of the Gaza Strip. According to a joint statement, Diab was killed in an airstrike carried out Wednesday in the Khan Yunis area. The Popular Resistance Committees, established in 2000, was previously affiliated with Fatah but is now linked to the Hamas and Hezbollah terrorist organizations, as well as Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Members of the organization participated in the October 7, 2023, massacre, infiltrating Israeli territory, murdering civilians and soldiers, and abducting Israelis into the Gaza Strip. Throughout the war, the organization carried out numerous terrorist attacks against IDF troops in cooperation with Hamas. According to the IDF and Shin Bet, Diab was involved in advancing terrorist attacks against Israeli soldiers and civilians throughout the war, including in recent months. He also worked to rebuild Hamas' military capabilities, in what the security agencies described as a systematic violation of the ceasefire agreement. The IDF said the airstrike was carried out to eliminate the threat posed by Diab. Prior to the strike, the military took measures to minimize the risk of civilian casualties, including the use of precision munitions and aerial surveillance.

citations.title: Report: Israel tells US Hamas doesn’t plan to disarm and is rebuilding its forces
citations.excerpt: Senior Israeli military officials have presented intelligence to their US counterparts that indicates Hamas has no intention of disarming and is instead rebuilding its forces in the Gaza Strip in preparation for possible renewed fighting, the Haaretz daily reported Thursday. Citing sources familiar with the information, the outlet reported that there is no intelligence indicating that Hamas has a set date to restart fighting or that it has developed an organized operational plan. The sources, however, reportedly described the assessment that the Palestinian terror group would not voluntarily surrender its weapons as “unequivocal.” The intelligence from the Israel Defense Forces and the Shin Bet was presented to American military officers, as well as to Israel’s political leadership, in recent days, as the administration of US President Donald Trump exerts pressure to implement a Gaza peace plan. According to the report, the IDF believes Hamas will not hand over its weapons to an international body, and can only be disarmed through military operations, including entering areas of Gaza not currently under Israel’s control. It also said Hamas has stockpiles of weapons in areas where the IDF did not conduct ground operations throughout the war, in part because of concerns that hostages were being held there. The military added that Hamas has restored much of its tunnel network in areas outside Israeli control and, according to Haaretz, has some 30,000 to 40,000 operatives. Israeli security officials said that Hamas has reestablished its governing authority in Gaza and faces no significant challenge to its rule there.

citations.title: Israeli attacks in Gaza kill four, including a young girl
citations.excerpt: Israeli attacks across Gaza have killed four Palestinians, including a young girl, in the past 24 hours as the Israeli military continues to seize more territory inside the enclave. The deaths on Thursday included a young girl who was killed by Israeli gunfire in northern Gaza near the Jabalia refugee camp, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. Al Jazeera’s Hani Mahmoud, reporting from Gaza City, said a strike on a vehicle in Gaza City’s Tal al-Hawa neighbourhood killed one person and seriously injured another. A separate strike killed a man on a bicycle in the southern city of Khan Younis. Meanwhile, the Gaza Health Ministry reported that a fourth person had died on Thursday of wounds sustained earlier in an Israeli strike. At least 1,538 Palestinians have been killed and 5,498 injured since the “ceasefire” took effect in October last year, according to the Gaza Health Ministry. Israel has killed more than 74,400 Palestinians in Gaza since October 2023. This comes amid warnings from a rights group that Gaza could face another famine as Israeli restrictions on incoming goods leave residents struggling to obtain food.

passages.text: Israeli forces continued targeted operations in the Gaza Strip against Hamas-linked elements, including the elimination of a senior Popular Resistance Committees commander, while intelligence assessments indicated ongoing Hamas rearmament in violation of the year-old ceasefire arrangements.

The IDF announced the elimination of Ramadan Muhammad Ashahada Diab in a precision strike in Khan Yunis, describing him as advancing attacks and restoring Hamas military capabilities systematically violating the ceasefire.
Separately, Palestinian medics reported three to four deaths from Israeli fire across Gaza, while the IDF stated it had struck Hamas militants in multiple locations.

Israeli security agencies maintain that continued operations are necessary to remove immediate threats from rearming terrorist elements, as Hamas is assessed to have no intention of voluntary disarmament and has restored significant tunnel and operational capacity.

Monitor further IDF statements on strike outcomes and any escalation in reported ceasefire violations, as well as US responses to the intelligence assessment on Hamas rebuilding ahead of Israeli elections.
